baseline: Waymo about 500,000 a week (March 2026); Apollo Go a peak above 300,000 a week (Q4 2025).
claim: By the end of 2028, Waymo or Apollo Go will report one and a half million fully driverless paid rides in a single week.
resolution: RIGHT if Waymo (Alphabet) or Apollo Go (Baidu) states, in an official disclosure, earnings release or on-the-record executive statement, at least 1,500,000 fully driverless paid rides in one calendar week falling on or before 2028-12-31. Rides with a safety driver do not count.
title: The Car Is a Room

claim: By the end of 2030, the US Census Bureau will count more than half a million people living in an RV, boat or van.
resolution: RIGHT if any American Community Survey 1-year estimate published on or before 2030-12-31 shows more than 500,000 people in occupied housing units of the type "Boat, RV, van, etc." (table B25033 or its successor).
title: The Car Is a Room

baseline: 46 percent in 2022/23; 62 percent in inner London.
claim: By the end of 2032, more than half of London households will have no car.
resolution: RIGHT if any edition of Transport for London's London Travel Demand Survey, or Travel in London report drawing on it, published on or before 2032-12-31 shows more than 50 percent of London households without access to a car.
title: The Car Is a Room

baseline: No such fare exists as of September 2026.
claim: By the end of 2030, an operator of driverless vehicles will sell a fare with the word sleep, overnight or rest in its name or official description.
resolution: RIGHT if, on or before 2030-12-31, a commercial operator of fully driverless passenger vehicles offers the public a bookable fare or product whose name or official description contains "sleep", "overnight" or "rest" (or the direct equivalent in the local language), in a city of more than one million people. A press stunt that the public cannot book does not count.
